hook: Lava crept down a neighborhood street, setting plants on fire.
narration: This lava was creeping down a street in a Hawaii neighborhood.
It was Kaupili Street in Leilani Estates, Hawaii, in May 2018.
A new crack in the ground, called fissure 21, was feeding it.
This kind of lava is called pahoehoe. Its surface cools into a skin, and fresh lava keeps breaking out from underneath.
The evening before, it had oozed up and over a berm.
Smoke rose as the asphalt under the flow started to burn.
Plants at the edge caught fire as it reached them.
outcome: The flow oozed right onto Kaupili Street and kept moving down the road.
title: Lava creeps down a Hawaii street
question_comment: How close would you get to a lava flow like this?

extra_sources.excerpt: Fissure 21 produced a Pāhoehoe lava flow that oozed onto Kaupili Street in the Leilani Estates subdivision.

description:
During the 2018 Kilauea eruption, a pahoehoe lava flow from fissure 21 oozed onto Kaupili Street in the Leilani Estates subdivision on Hawaii Island, May 24 and 25, 2018.
